previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease stage III, and a history of recurrent gastroparesis was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, consistent with a gastroparesis flare triggered by poor glycemic control and a new burning epigastric sensation suggestive of GERD. Her blood glucose was initially very high at 691, requiring IV insulin, but was stabilized with her home NPH regimen. Hypertension and transient worsening of kidney function were noted but improved with hydration and continued use of lisinopril. She was started on omeprazole for suspected acid reflux, which may have been contributing to her symptoms. Her pain and nausea were managed with oxycodone and lorazepam, avoiding contraindicated medications due to allergies. A multidisciplinary care plan involving her PCP, psychiatrist, and social work was established to reduce future admissions. She improved clinically, advanced to a soft diet, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans and a new prescription for omeprazole.
